Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated `/_framework/debug` endpoint used by `dotnet watch`. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "Compiler output cache drops warnings and changes MSBuild -warnaserror results" (#86198) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
The experimental compiler output cache drops warnings on cache hits. With MSBuild's engine-level `-warnaserror`, the compiler can succeed while the build fails. The server caches that result, so the next identical rebuild incorrectly succeeds.

**Version Used**: .NET SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`, C# compiler `5.11.0-1.26420.103`, Linux x64.

**Steps to Reproduce**:

In a fresh directory, create `CacheWarningRepro.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>
    <UseSharedCompilation>true</UseSharedCompilation>
    <Features>use-global-cache=$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)compiler-cache</Features>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

And `C.cs`:

```csharp
public class C
{
    [System.Obsolete("Example warning")]
    public static void Old() { }

    public static void M() => Old();
}
```

Run the same command twice:

```sh
dotnet build -t:Rebuild -warnaserror
dotnet build -t:Rebuild -warnaserror
```

**Diagnostic Id**: `CS0618`.

**Expected Behavior**: Both rebuilds fail with `CS0618` promoted to an error.

**Actual Behavior**: The first rebuild fails with exit code 1. The second restores the compiler outputs from cache, reports no warnings or errors, and succeeds with exit code 0. Both invocations reach the compiler server; this is not MSBuild's incremental target skipping.

This is distinct from compiler-owned `TreatWarningsAsErrors`: MSBuild applies its policy after receiving the compiler result. Replaying the original compiler warnings on cache hits would preserve that downstream decision without including MSBuild warning policy in the compiler cache key.

> *This content was created with assistance from AI.*

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
`dotnet sln list` command output can't be used directly as a text file for automation because of the header.

``` sh
dotnet sln source.sln list | xargs dotnet sln destination.sln add
```

It won't work, because of the very useful header:

``` txt
Project(s)
----------
```

One possible workaround for command line would be:

``` sh
dotnet sln source.sln list | tail -3
```

### Describe the solution you'd like
Drop the header from the output.
If solution is empty, don't output anything. Return exactly one line per project.
Alternatively, provide a machine friendly format option, such as ```--format json```

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Best Regards,

Raphael

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Compiler output cache drops warnings and changes MSBuild -warnaserror results
Issues.Body:
The experimental compiler output cache drops warnings on cache hits. With MSBuild's engine-level `-warnaserror`, the compiler can succeed while the build fails. The server caches that result, so the next identical rebuild incorrectly succeeds.

**Version Used**: .NET SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`, C# compiler `5.11.0-1.26420.103`, Linux x64.

**Steps to Reproduce**:

In a fresh directory, create `CacheWarningRepro.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>
    <UseSharedCompilation>true</UseSharedCompilation>
    <Features>use-global-cache=$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)compiler-cache</Features>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

And `C.cs`:

```csharp
public class C
{
    [System.Obsolete("Example warning")]
    public static void Old() { }

    public static void M() => Old();
}
```

Run the same command twice:

```sh
dotnet build -t:Rebuild -warnaserror
dotnet build -t:Rebuild -warnaserror
```

**Diagnostic Id**: `CS0618`.

**Expected Behavior**: Both rebuilds fail with `CS0618` promoted to an error.

**Actual Behavior**: The first rebuild fails with exit code 1. The second restores the compiler outputs from cache, reports no warnings or errors, and succeeds with exit code 0. Both invocations reach the compiler server; this is not MSBuild's incremental target skipping.

This is distinct from compiler-owned `TreatWarningsAsErrors`: MSBuild applies its policy after receiving the compiler result. Replaying the original compiler warnings on cache hits would preserve that downstream decision without including MSBuild warning policy in the compiler cache key.

> *This content was created with assistance from AI.*
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Compiler output cache drops warnings and changes MSBuild -warnaserror results" (#86198)

Issues.Title: Investigate eliminating unused synthesized struct `this` loads in async methods
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to the extra-load discussion on dotnet/roslyn#86134.

An async struct method can emit a load of `this` even when its source body never references the receiver:

```csharp
struct S
{
    public async Task<int> M(int value)
    {
        await Task.Delay(1);
        return value;
    }
}
```

With runtime-async lowering, the method starts with:

```il
ldarg.0
ldobj S
pop
```

`RuntimeAsyncRewriter.hoistThisIfNeeded` synthesizes a copy of the struct receiver. With the changes in dotnet/roslyn#86134, removing the unused local preserves the dereference, leaving this load behind. The PR discussion also identifies analogous receiver copying in traditional async lowering.

We should investigate whether compiler-generated receiver reads can be distinguished from reads required by user code, allowing unnecessary loads to be optimized away.

The investigation should:
- Cover runtime-async and traditional state-machine lowering.
- Preserve dereferences corresponding to source-level reads, including an explicit `_ = this;`.
- Add focused IL and execution coverage for whichever optimizations are safe.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Investigate eliminating unused synthesized struct `this` loads in async methods" (#86195)

Issues.Title: CS8629 and CS8604 are reported despite null checks after three left joins in query syntax
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: 
.NET SDK 10.0.401  
C# compiler/MSBuild 18.9.11+e34a38d2ae  

**Description**:
Nullable flow analysis reports `CS8629: Nullable value type may be null` and `CS8604: Possible null reference argument for parameter` for nullable property accesses guarded by not-null checks in a LINQ query expression after three chained left joins.

The same query expressed with the corresponding LINQ method calls produces neither of the two warnings.

When the query is reduced to one or two chained left joins, the warnings are not produced.

**Steps to Reproduce**:
```csharp

#nullable enable

using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

public sealed class Item
{
	public int Id { get; init; }
	public int? A { get; init; }
	public string? B { get; init; }
}

public sealed record Pair(int A, string B);

public static class Repro
{
	public static IEnumerable<Pair?> QuerySyntax(
		IEnumerable<int> ids,
		IEnumerable<Item> items,
		IEnumerable<int> first,
		IEnumerable<int> second) =>
		from id in ids
		join item in items on id equals item.Id into itemGroup
		from item in itemGroup.DefaultIfEmpty()
		join a in first on item.Id equals a into firstGroup
		from a in firstGroup.DefaultIfEmpty()
		join b in second on a equals b into secondGroup
		from b in secondGroup.DefaultIfEmpty()
		select item.A != null && item.B != null
			? new Pair(item.A.Value, item.B) // CS8629 and CS8604
			: null;

	public static IEnumerable<Pair?> MethodSyntax(
		IEnumerable<int> ids,
		IEnumerable<Item> items,
		IEnumerable<int> first,
		IEnumerable<int> second) =>
		ids
			.GroupJoin(
				items,
				id => id,
				item => item.Id,
				(id, itemGroup) => new { id, itemGroup })
			.SelectMany(
				x => x.itemGroup.DefaultIfEmpty(),
				(x, item) => new { item })
			.GroupJoin(
				first,
				x => x.item!.Id,
				a => a,
				(x, firstGroup) => new { x.item, firstGroup })
			.SelectMany(
				x => x.firstGroup.DefaultIfEmpty(),
				(x, a) => new { x.item, a })
			.GroupJoin(
				second,
				x => x.a,
				b => b,
				(x, secondGroup) => new { x.item, secondGroup })
			.SelectMany(
				x => x.secondGroup.DefaultIfEmpty(),
				(x, _) => x.item)
			.Select(item => item!.A != null && item.B != null
				? new Pair(item.A.Value, item.B) // no diagnostics
				: null);
}
```

**Diagnostic Id**:
CS8629: Nullable value type may be null.
CS8604: Possible null reference argument for parameter

**Expected Behavior**:
Compiling should not produce a warning because the properties are checked for null.

**Actual Behavior**:
Compiling produces two warnings:
> warning CS8629: Nullable value type may be null.
> warning CS8604: Possible null reference argument for parameter
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "CS8629 and CS8604 are reported despite null checks after three left joins in query syntax" (#86188)

Issues.Title: Enable persistent Roslyn indices for project-discovery workspaces
Issues.Body:
Roslyn persistent storage is enabled when a workspace is opened from a solution file, but disabled when the workspace is created by discovering and opening individual project files.


`LanguageServerProjectSystem.OpenSolutionAsync` assigns the solution path used to create a stable persistent-storage key. `OpenProjectsAsync` does not assign a solution path. As a result, `DefaultPersistentStorageConfiguration.TryGetStorageLocation` returns `null`, and Roslyn cannot persist `SyntaxTreeIndex` or `TopLevelSyntaxTreeIndex` data.


This causes project-discovery workspaces to rebuild search indices in each new process. In testing, an indexed query against a project-only workspace did not create or modify a `storage.ide` database. Opening the same projects through an `.slnx` file persisted the indices, and a subsequent process successfully loaded them.


Project-discovery workspaces should receive a stable persistent-storage identity. This could be implemented by assigning a synthetic solution path or by deriving a cache key from the workspace root and discovered project set. The identity must remain stable across processes and change when the project set changes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Enable persistent Roslyn indices for project-discovery workspaces" (#86183)

Issues.Title: ProjectData: importing SDK and tooling copies duplicates properties in .lscache files
Issues.Body:
## Description

When C# Dev Kit generates ProjectData for a solution on macOS, the SDK and tooling can both import `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.targets`. Both copies import their adjacent `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Schema.props`, whose additive `_ProjectDataProperties` items then accumulate twice. This can result in duplicate properties in generated `.lscache` files.

The SDK already imports its ProjectData targets when present. The tooling also injects its separate copy through `CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets` (and `CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonCrossTargetingTargets` for outer builds).

## Reproduction

With .NET SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`, create a minimal SDK-style project targeting `net10.0`, then evaluate its ProjectData properties:

```sh
dotnet msbuild Example.csproj -nologo -getItem:_ProjectDataProperties
```

With only the SDK import, this produces 18 items with 18 unique identities. Evaluate again with a separate copy of the ProjectData targets and schema injected via `CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets`:

```sh
dotnet msbuild Example.csproj -nologo -getItem:_ProjectDataProperties \
  -p:CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets=/absolute/path/to/separate/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.targets
```

Using matching targets and schema files, this produces 36 items with 18 unique identities (each identity appears twice). This evaluation-only reproduction confirms the duplicate input items; it does not establish that writer tasks execute twice. The full C# Dev Kit scenario has been observed to produce duplicate properties in `.lscache` files.

## Expected behavior

The SDK and tooling copies should coexist with defined precedence and without duplicate schema items or serialized cache properties. Regression coverage should exercise imports from distinct physical copies of the targets/schema files.

## Related work

[dotnet/roslyn#86094](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86094) addresses generation of the ProjectData schema properties file. It appears separate from this duplicate-import case: its generated schema entries remain additive, and the issue described here is caused by both physical imports contributing the same items.

## References

- [Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.targets](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/src/ProjectData/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks/build/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.targets)
- [Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Schema.props](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/src/ProjectData/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks/build/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Schema.props)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "ProjectData: importing SDK and tooling copies duplicates properties in .lscache files" (#86182)

Issues.Title: Fix build-failure analysis Responses API routing
Issues.Body:
The build-failure analysis workflows select `gpt-6.1-sol`, but AWF v0.28.10 only automatically selects the Responses wire API for GPT-5 and o3 models. Consequently, Copilot sends requests to `/chat/completions` and receives `400 model "gpt-6.1-sol" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint` before analyzing any binlogs.

Set `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API: responses` in the shared workflow frontmatter and regenerate both the automatic and maintainer-command workflow locks with the existing gh-aw v0.87.10 compiler. This preserves the configured model, permissions, firewall isolation, and safe-output behavior.

Related to #86174. Reproducing run: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/actions/runs/39741024061/job/119699440739

The separate upstream bug that reports a skipped threat-detection run as `agent_failure` is outside this change. The production workflow has not been rerun with this configuration.

Issues.Title: Reduce allocations during remote asset synchronization
Issues.Body:
Remote asset synchronization can allocate a 16 KB temporary checksum array to request just one missing asset. These arrays hold asset identifiers, not document contents.

The old pool retained 16 arrays of 1,024 checksums each, and each request kept its array until the asynchronous fetch finished. Overlapping requests could exhaust that pool and force fresh 16 KB allocations. Single-asset requests now rent a small size bucket (16 or 32 checksums in the probe, about 256-512 bytes of checksum storage), reducing the temporary memory needed for each outstanding request.

With both pools warmed, an isolated .NET Framework 4.8 probe of 64 overlapping single-asset cache misses reduced median request-setup allocations from 888,472 to 100,944 bytes (89%). This benefit targets bursts: warmed, non-overlapping requests could already reuse the old buffers without allocating replacement arrays.

Asset selection, serialized data volume, and RPC count are unchanged; the measurement does not cover transfer or serialization cost or end-to-end Razor performance.

Issues.Title: [aw] Detection Runs
Issues.Body:
This issue tracks all runs where threat detection flagged problems in agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a detection warning or failure posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows where threat detection raised concerns
- Review patterns of detection warnings or failures
- Identify false positives or recurring issues with threat detection
- Monitor the health of the threat detection system

</details>

<details>
<summary>Resources</summary>

- [GitHub Agentic Workflows Documentation](https://github.com/github/gh-aw)

</details>

> [!TIP]
> To configure threat detection behavior, update the frontmatter:
> ```yaml
> safe-outputs:
>   threat-detection:
>     continue-on-error: true   # Warnings only (default)
>     # continue-on-error: false  # Strict mode — block safe outputs
> ```

---

Issues.Title: Reduce LSP JSON JIT with generated protocol metadata
Issues.Body:
System.Text.Json creates protocol contracts and converter specializations dynamically, adding JIT work when the language server handles requests.

Use generated metadata and statically constructed converters across Roslyn's protocol surface, including executable-host and Razor contracts, with no reflection resolver fallback. Additional contracts must supply generated metadata. Preserve wire formats, progress notifications, polymorphism, and error serialization, with coverage checks for missing registrations across component boundaries.

Issues.Title: dotnetup init: label the platform-recommended access mode separately from the preselected configured mode
Issues.Body:
## Problem

When dotnetup is already configured, `dotnetup init` preselects the configured access mode and labels it `(default)`. For example, if `dotnetup.config.json` contains `"accessMode": "none"`, the form shows `None  (default)` on Windows, even though the platform default for new setups on Windows is `Everywhere`.

This happens because `InitDefaultsResolver.GetDefaultAccessMode` gives a supported configured mode priority over the platform default. `InitFormModel.BuildAccessModeField` then uses that mode as the field's `DefaultIndex`, which is rendered with the `(default)` suffix. Users who reconfigure can't tell which mode dotnetup recommends for their platform.

## Proposal

Keep preselecting the configured mode, so accepting the form without edits preserves the current setup. Label the two modes separately:

- `(current)` on the configured mode
- `(recommended)` on the platform default (`Everywhere` on Windows; `Shell` elsewhere when a supported shell is detected, otherwise `None`)

When the two are the same, show a single label. "Changed from default" highlighting should compare against the current (preselected) mode.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dotnetup init: label the platform-recommended access mode separately from the preselected configured mode" (#56765)

Issues.Title: Keep Razor shadow copies private to the current user
Issues.Body:
Razor build servers cache extension assemblies outside their source directories. Those copies need to retain the source directory's user boundary.

Use the Unix user-local data directory instead of shared temporary storage, and create the shadow-copy tree with owner-only permissions. Keep the Windows location unchanged and fail if no user-local root is available. Dispose the directory-lifetime mutex without trying to release ownership the manager never acquires.

Keep the implementation local to the legacy Razor server. Cover assembly and satellite-resource copies, an existing permissive base directory, and directory-lifetime cleanup.

Issues.Title: Delete stale RID-specific assets file between local tool restores
Issues.Body:
The order in which I declared my tools in the dotnet-tools.json should not matter. But it did. With `aspire.cli` listed before `csharpier` in `dotnet-tools.json`, a fresh restore fails. The error says the `csharpier` package only contains `aspire`.

I tasked Claude to fix this bug, and this is the result.

The bug is in `dotnet tool restore`. Every local tool in one restore shares one asset directory. A RID-specific tool like _aspire.cli_ leaves `project.assets.ridpackage.json` behind. The next tool, _csharpier_, picks it up and fails.

A helper in `ToolPackageDownloaderBase.cs` deletes that stale file before the next tool's assets are written. A manual restore with the patched build succeeded for both tools.

Issues.Title: OpenHarmony: apply the sandbox defaults to the SDK tools
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Bake the OpenHarmony sandbox defaults (JIT W^X off, invariant globalization) into the SDK tools' runtimeconfigs, and keep the telemetry/logo opt-outs for the CLI's child processes. User applications keep their own defaults.

Stacked on #56733 (SDK build enablement).

## Changes

- The sandbox defaults are written into the SDK tools' runtimeconfigs: the redist runtimeconfig carries `System.Runtime.EnableWriteXorExecute=false` and `System.Globalization.Invariant=true` for `dotnet`, `MSBuild` and `NuGet.CommandLine.XPlat`, and `UpdateRuntimeConfig` injects the same options into every other tool runtimeconfig (csc, VBCSCompiler, F#).
- `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaults` only sets `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` / `DOTNET_NOLOGO=1` on OpenHarmony; they only affect the SDK's child processes.
- TMPDIR is deliberately not set: the runtime reads the host-provided value through `Path.GetTempPath()`.
- Tests: `UpdateRuntimeConfigTests` covers the runtimeconfig injection; `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaultsTests` pins the two remaining CLI defaults.

## Why runtimeconfig, not environment variables

`System.Runtime.EnableWriteXorExecute` and `System.Globalization.Invariant` are per-process runtime options. Writing them into the SDK tool runtimeconfigs keeps them scoped to the SDK's tools; setting them in the environment would propagate to every child process, including user applications.

## Test

1. Run the SDK on OHOS: the CLI, MSBuild, csc, VBCSCompiler and F# work without external environment variables; their runtimeconfigs contain the two sandbox defaults, while a user application's runtimeconfig is unchanged.
2. `UpdateRuntimeConfigTests` and `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaultsTests` pass.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was authored with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Issues.Title: OpenHarmony: sign build and publish outputs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Adds the build/publish signing hook for OpenHarmony: the `OpenHarmonyCodesign` MSBuild task and the `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets` wiring that signs the apphost after build and the ELF outputs after publish for `openharmony-*` RIDs.

Stacked on #56735 (ELF signer and `dotnet selfsign`).

## Changes

- `OpenHarmonyCodesign` task: signs ELF64 files in place in the given directories; no-op for non-ELF files; does not follow symbolic links; keeps an existing `.codesign` section written by another signer; skips files whose self-signature is still valid.
- `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets`: `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignBuildOutputs` signs the apphost after build; `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignPublishOutputs` signs the publish output; both only for `openharmony-*` RIDs.
- NETSDK1247-1250 diagnostics and xlf.

## API

The task is public because MSBuild `UsingTask` requires a public type. Proposal: dotnet/sdk#56759. It is an implementation detail of the targets, not a supported library API.

## Validation

- On device, the apphost and publish outputs are signed and execute; an unsigned or modified binary fails with `EPERM`.
- The signer itself is covered by the tests in #56735.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was drafted with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Issues.Title: API proposal: OpenHarmonyCodesign MSBuild task
Issues.Body:
## Background

OpenHarmony devices only execute ELF binaries that carry a valid `.codesign` section, and a signed binary whose content changes fails with `EPERM`. The SDK therefore has to re-sign the apphost and the native outputs after build/publish for `openharmony-*` RIDs.

dotnet/sdk#56735 adds the ELF signer and the `dotnet selfsign` command; dotnet/sdk#56760 adds the targets hook that uses the signer. This issue is the API proposal for the one new public type that the hook needs.

## Proposed API

```csharp
namespace Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks;

public sealed class OpenHarmonyCodesign : TaskBase
{
    [Required]
    public string[] Directories { get; set; }
}
```

- Assembly: `Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.dll`
- The task walks each directory, signs the ELF64 files in place, and is a no-op for non-ELF files.
- It does not follow symbolic links (file or directory links), keeps an existing `.codesign` section created by another signer, and skips files whose self-signature is still valid.

## Why it is public

MSBuild's `UsingTask` mechanism requires the task type to be public. The type is an implementation detail of `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets`; it is only used by `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignBuildOutputs` and `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignPublishOutputs` for `openharmony-*` runtime identifiers. It is not intended as a supported library API and carries no API compatibility guarantee.

## Alternatives considered

- **`dotnet selfsign` command only** (the command is added in #56735): the build/publish hook would have to `Exec` the CLI for every build. That adds a process launch per build and is not how the SDK invokes its build hooks; macOS codesigning is part of the `CreateAppHost` task.
- **Make the task internal**: MSBuild requires a public task type.

## Compatibility / lifetime

The task can be made internal or removed if the SDK team prefers a different shape; the user-facing force path is the `dotnet selfsign` command, which is independent of this task.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Issues.Title: Generate fixed size buffers as fixed fields in GenAPI
Issues.Body:
Fixes #31744

GenAPI wrote fixed size buffers the way they look in metadata, which doesn't compile. For

```cs
public struct Buffers
{
    public unsafe fixed int Values[64];
}
```

it produced:

```cs
[System.Runtime.CompilerServices.FixedBuffer(typeof(int), 64)]
public unsafe int* Values;
[System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CompilerGenerated]
[System.Runtime.CompilerServices.UnsafeValueType]
public partial struct <Values>e__FixedBuffer
{
    public int FixedElementField;
}
```

Now it writes `public unsafe fixed int Values[64];`:
- `DeclarationExt` builds the field from `IFieldSymbol.IsFixedSizeBuffer`/`FixedSize`: the element type of the pointer, `[FixedSize]` on the declarator, and the `fixed` modifier (plus `unsafe` if it's missing).
- `FixedBufferAttribute` is added to the reserved attributes. The compiler emits it for a `fixed` field and reports CS1716 if it's written in source.
- The compiler-generated `<Name>e__FixedBuffer` struct is skipped when the containing type has a fixed size buffer field with that name, including fields that are filtered out.

Test: `TestFixedBufferFieldGeneration` covers a public fixed buffer next to an internal one and a normal field. The internal buffer turns into the usual `_dummyPrimitive`. The test fails without this change.

`Microsoft.DotNet.GenAPI.Tests` locally: 108 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Generate fixed size buffers as fixed fields in GenAPI" (#56755)

Issues.Title: File-based apps: dotnet run reuses cached build when a required dependency DLL is missing
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

`dotnet run --file` reuses the cached build of a file-based app even when a required package dependency DLL is missing from the cached output directory. It then crashes with `FileNotFoundException`, instead of rebuilding/copying the missing dependency.

This was first observed with a small file-based utility referencing `NuGet.Configuration` and `NuGet.Packaging`. The cause of the original DLL disappearance is unknown. The following minimal repro deliberately removes one output DLL to demonstrate the cache-validation problem deterministically; it does not delete anything from the global NuGet package cache.

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows with PowerShell, create `repro.cs` in an otherwise empty directory:

```csharp
#:package NuGet.Configuration@7.3.1

Console.WriteLine(typeof(NuGet.Configuration.Settings).Assembly.Location);
```

Run:

```powershell
# Build and run successfully; capture the copied dependency's location.
$dll = dotnet run --file .\repro.cs | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll)) {
    throw "Initial run failed or dependency path was not found."
}

# Remove only this file-based app's copied dependency DLL.
# The path printed above is under:
# %TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\repro-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dll

# No source/input changes. This reuses the incomplete cache and crashes.
dotnet run --file .\repro.cs

# Force the build: succeeds and restores the missing DLL.
dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs
Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll # True
```

The `Assembly.Location` access may produce an IL3000 warning on the initial build; the normal `dotnet run` execution nevertheless prints the DLL's actual path. This exact minimal program was tested successfully before deleting the DLL, failed after deleting it, and succeeded again with `--no-cache`.

### Expected behavior

Without `--no-build`, `dotnet run --file` detects that a required runtime output is missing, invokes the build to restore it, and runs successfully. An incomplete cached build should not be considered up to date.

### Actual behavior

The second normal run skips the build and fails:

```text
Unhandled exception. System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'. The system cannot find the file specified.
File name: 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'
Requested by: sdk-missing-dependency-repro, Version=1.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null
 --> System.Private.CoreLib, Version=11.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args)
```

The host also reports that it cannot open `%TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\<app>-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll` with error `0x80070002`.

Exit code observed: `-532462766`.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown; verified with SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`. Other SDK versions have not been tested.

### Are there any workarounds?

Use `dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs`. This restores the missing DLL and runs successfully, but forces the build on every invocation.

### Environment

```text
.NET SDK:
 Version:         11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105
 Commit:          820230c386
 MSBuild version: 18.12.0-1.26504.105+820230c38

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:         Windows
 OS Version:      10.0.26300
 OS Platform:     Windows
 RID:             win-x64

Host:
 Version:         11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105
 Architecture:    x64
 Commit:          820230c386

Environment variables:
 DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD_TO_PRERELEASE=1

global.json:
 Not found
```

Reproduced from the command line without an IDE.

### Related issue

Possibly related symptoms: dotnet/sdk#53732. That issue was closed after a fix involving `#:project` dependency changes. This repro uses only a direct `#:package` reference, no referenced projects, no concurrent execution, and an explicitly removed runtime output on a newer SDK.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "File-based apps: dotnet run reuses cached build when a required dependency DLL is missing" (#56747)

Issues.Title: Add adaptive CI failure attribution skill
Issues.Body:
## Problem

A failing CI run can be caused by a recent change, an older issue, an occasional failure, or a problem with the build service. One retry or an older similar failure alone doesn't show which explanation is right.

## Description

Add a read-only skill that guides agents through CI failures. It helps them confirm which code and build were tested, look into each failure, and gather only the evidence needed to distinguish possible causes.

The skill also explains how to compare runs, describe confidence and evidence gaps, and avoid claiming that a change had no effect unless the evidence supports that conclusion.

Issues.Title: Backport distinct Copilot CLI and VS Code agent detection to .NET 10
Issues.Body:
## Problem

The .NET 10 `release/10.0.4xx` detector recognizes `COPILOT_CLI=1` but emits the legacy `copilot` label. It does not recognize the VS Code agent signals `COPILOT_AGENT` or `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent`.

Newer SDK code distinguishes `copilot-cli` from `copilot-vscode`. Backporting this distinction would improve detection coverage and make agent attribution consistent across SDK generations.

## Proposed change

Backport the Copilot-specific detection and label changes from #54358 and #54659 to the appropriate supported .NET 10 SDK servicing branches, without bringing in unrelated agent-detection changes. Emit `copilot-cli` for CLI signals and `copilot-vscode` for VS Code signals. Preserve the existing `copilot-app` detection backported in #55443 and the ability to report multiple matching agents.

Include coverage for CLI-only, VS Code-only, App, overlapping signals, and no-agent environments.

## Behavior considerations

This is not exclusively a telemetry change: detecting an agent also affects MSBuild live node display and Microsoft.Testing.Platform ANSI output. Validate and document those effects for newly recognized environments.

The backport only improves future reporting from updated SDKs. Consumers must continue handling the legacy `copilot` label; historical data cannot universally distinguish the clients because some earlier implementations used that label for both.

Related: #53032, #54348, #54276.

Issues.Title: Add SDK-generated fallback for the Hot Reload settings endpoint
Issues.Body:
Possible fix for https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/69718.

## Problem

After https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56118, .NET 11 SDK generates Blazor browser-tools initializers when Hot Reload build outputs are enabled (by default in Debug builds). This also happens for ordinary `dotnet run` launches and projects targeting older frameworks, since SDK selection is independent of the target framework.

When an initializer probes `/_framework/dotnet-browser-tools/hot-reload-settings.json`, older hosts lack the disabled-settings endpoint supplied by .NET 11 ASP.NET Core hosts. The initializer correctly treats the failed request as Hot Reload being disabled, but the browser still reports a 404.

## Change

For pre-.NET 11 targets, generate a constant `{"hotReload": false}` static asset at the existing settings URL. Generation uses the existing browser-tools gate, including `EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile`. The asset is build-only, excluded from publish output, and reused without rewriting on incremental builds.

Net11+ targets continue using their existing host fallback. Their non-Development behavior is unchanged.

## Behavior preservation

- **Active watch providers retain precedence.** ASP.NET Core and legacy DevServer forwarding runs before static assets. Gateway’s provider proxy uses order `-1000`, ahead of static asset endpoints at `-100`.
- **No activation state is written into build output.** The generated file always contains `false`. The provider supplies `true` dynamically, preserving the same build output across ordinary and watch launches.
- **Default Release and publish behavior remain unchanged.** The fallback follows the existing Hot Reload generation gate and never reaches published applications.

## Validation

All Web/WASM regression cases covering net8 and net10 fail without the fix and pass with it. All 32 focused integration tests and 12 real-browser run/watch scenarios pass, including state-preserving live edits.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add SDK-generated fallback for the Hot Reload settings endpoint" (#56743)

Issues.Title: Warn when targeting .NET 11 in Visual Studio 18.11 or earlier
Issues.Body:
Targeting .NET 11 in Visual Studio 2026 18.11 or earlier is unsupported, but the SDK currently only reports the older .NET 10/VS 17 compatibility warning. This adds the equivalent warning for .NET 11, following the approach in #51366.

- Emit NETSDK1245 for .NETCoreApp 11.0 or higher when MSBuild is older than 18.12.0.
- Preserve the existing .NET 10/VS 17 warning and regenerate all 13 localization files through the build.
- Add 15 compatibility boundary cases covering older engines, VS 18.11 servicing versions, the 18.12 cutoff, newer frameworks, and unaffected framework identifiers.

## Validation

All 18 focused tests passed: 15 compatibility cases, two diagnostic-code integrity tests, and one ILLink smoke test. Formatting verification and `git diff --check` passed.

Full-build validation encountered unrelated missing Template Engine approval files. A direct redist build also reported two missing ASP.NET analyzer localization files, but produced the current SDK targets and task assemblies used successfully by the focused tests.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96960 | .NET and Visual Studio Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Runtime. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. DateTime Hebrew-number parsing can read outside expected stack bounds and terminate the process. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96232 | .NET and Visual Studio Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Restrictive XAML and XPS security fixes block unsafe URI fetching and navigation, propagate untrusted-input state through hyperlink navigation, add TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits, and avoid caching positive DNS zone-policy decisions. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/12024 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96231 | .NET and Visual Studio Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime; System.Private.CoreLib. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Unix named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symlink races, and unsafe permission changes, allowing local attackers to truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions, or elevate privileges. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135707 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70194 | .NET and Visual Studio Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Net.Security. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. .NET 11 post-handshake TLS client authentication can fail to verify the client certificate, allowing mutual-authentication requirements to be bypassed. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135701 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Moderate - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-295 (Improper Certificate Validation) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70190 | .NET SDK Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK workload installation and advertising manifests. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The elevated SDK workload installer can follow a junction or symlink under `%ProgramData%\dotnet`, enabling local privilege escalation. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56612 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- .NET SDK | >= 11.0.100-preview.1, <= 11.0.100-rc.1 | 11.0.100-rc.2 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.401 | 10.0.402 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.112 | 10.0.113 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
